//2: buggy_repair is deliberately absent from every autoApprove list below. It writes nothing, but a patch is a change to your code and deserves a human glance.

buggy.//: Use this when the package is installed and on PATH.

buggy-venv.//: Recommended. An absolute path into a virtualenv needs no PATH changes, and sidesteps the TypeScript package, which installs a binary with the same name. Create it with: python3 -m venv ~/.buggy-venv && ~/.buggy-venv/bin/pip install -e /path/to/debugger/buggy-py

buggy-from-source.//: No install at all - runs straight from a checkout. Replace the path with your own.
buggy-from-source.//2: The path is passed as a literal to -c rather than through PYTHONPATH on purpose. PYTHONPATH is colon-separated on POSIX, so a checkout whose path contains a colon silently becomes two directories that do not exist, and the server fails with ModuleNotFoundError. A repr'd argument is immune to that, and to spaces.
args: import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/absolute/path/to/debugger/buggy-py'); from buggy import mcp; sys.exit(mcp.main())
